Fixes bug B-main-red-brief-wording: Heading is now ## RESUME: recoverable work found; tests search the old text or an order the brief no longer has. 7 of the 288 failing ids on main 057a4a6b0 (gate event ee9be0cdf3faaebca2413c9b5), grouped by error text: test_brief_budget_sections.py::test_a_tiny_budget_is_still_a_budget, test_brief_recovery_all.py::test_a_running_item_with_no_lease_is_in_the_brief, test_brief_recovery_all.py::test_an_unmeasurable_worktree_is_in_the_brief, test_brief_recovery_all.py::test_salvageable_work_still_comes_first_and_clean_leftovers_are_counted, test_decisions_recall.py::test_status_surfaces_loops_and_recoverable_work, test_session_start_resume.py::test_the_brief_itself_puts_recoverable_work_before_new_work, test_session_start_resume.py::test_the_session_start_output_opens_with_the_resume_block

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-main-red-brief-wording --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-main-red-brief-wording --regression-test <test>` first).

Scope measured by red-d at 164ff741b: 8 failures, not 7 (test_recovery_plan.py::test_plain_recover_is_unchanged_on_a_clean_project joins, from Be3461fc98e). tests/test_recovery_plan.py and ddflow/views/markdown/briefing.py added to the globs. The two test_session_start_resume.py failures need ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py, held by B-hy-stop-protocol and PS-git-batch: see the follow-up task.

data.note: Per-test verdicts: stale expectations fixed in tests, a silent empty brief fixed in the view; RESUME order waits for brief.py

data.claim: Six failures are stale test expectations against deliberate shipped behaviour, one of which also exposes a silent empty brief; two are real order bugs in api.lifecycle.brief.
data.falsifier: The six tests still failing after only their expectations change, or the two order tests passing without a brief.py change.
data.mechanism: DX-recover-brief-slice renamed the heading and made the prefix uncuttable; f605f7d7a refuses unknown --needs; exit-2 outcomes print their reason on stdout (pinned by test_uc_surf_reporting_recover); api.brief prepends blocks after the view has placed RESUME first.
data.probe: git archive of merge 12cae2ff0 and pytest there; then on the worktree pytest of the target files; a scratch copy with the hoist in brief.py running test_session_start_resume, test_brief_recovery_slice, test_brief_recovery_all, test_flow, test_lines
data.probe_output: At 12cae2ff0: 6 failed, 6 passed (the same session-start, tiny-budget and recovery-all ids: red since the merge that wrote them). Worktree: 67 passed across budget, slice, recovery_all, decisions_recall, recovery_plan. Scratch copy with the hoist: first try above review feedback failed tests/test_flow.py:421, so feedback stays first; second try 98 passed.
data.question: For each of the 8 failures, is the code or the test expectation wrong?

data.summary: views.markdown.brief opens with the RESUME slice (DX-recover-brief-slice: a session after a crash must see recoverable work first), but api.lifecycle.brief then prepends the Open workflow choices, reports and contest blocks above it, so on any project with an undecided flow knob the first section is not RESUME. tests/test_session_start_resume.py (test_the_brief_itself_puts_recoverable_work_before_new_work, test_the_session_start_output_opens_with_the_resume_block) have been red since the DX-recover-brief-slice merge 12cae2ff0. Those tests are right; the code is wrong. The fix needs ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py, held by B-hy-stop-protocol and PS-git-batch. A 9-line fix hoisting the slice above those blocks but under Review feedback, which tests/test_flow.py pins first, passed 98 tests in a scratch copy.

evidence.note: R8dbb288632 CONFIRMED: at merge 12cae2ff0 6 of the ids were already red, so these tests failed from the merge that wrote them. Per test: 3 recovery_all stale wording; decisions_recall stale since f605f7d7a refuses unknown --needs; recovery_plan stale since exit 2 prints its reason on stdout; tiny budget stale in that the head now holds, with a real gap fixed in the view; 2 session-start tests right, code wrong, moved to B-brief-choices-above-resume.

Read the brief and `ddflow decision applicable`; recall on the budget and RESUME topic. Governing: D-recovery-one-design and D-orphan-recovery (RESUME slice never cut: the prefix still holds), D-small-files-30k (briefing.py 29920 bytes, under the limit), r-bounded-everything (the note makes the cut visible; the overrun is bounded by the note's length), r-task-phase-needs-wave (follow-up in P-green-main, tag no-deps, wave stamped).

chunk_findings.detail: The changed assertion requires the text `"## Current: T9"`, but this changeset does not update `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py`; current code still emits `"## Suggested next: T9"` (the change description itself says this test stays red). Running the test with the existing fixture causes `text.index("## Current: T9")` to raise `ValueError`, so the suite fails.
